analysis.investment_thesis: Anant Raj has executed an impressive recovery from near-zero profits in 2021 to INR 426 Cr net profit in 2025, and its data-centre pivot adds a high-quality growth vector, but with an earnings yield of only ~2.6% (EBIT INR 492 Cr / EV ~INR 18,628 Cr) and ROCE of just 11.2%, neither leg of the Magic Formula is satisfied. Hold if already owned for the data-centre optionality, but do not initiate by formula.
key_strengths: Dramatic deleveraging: borrowings fell from INR 1,691 Cr (2020) to INR 563 Cr (2025), transforming the balance sheet and freeing up interest expense
Revenue and profit compounding strongly: revenue 9Y CAGR 19%, net profit CAGR 22.2% with 2025 profits 5x the 2021 trough
Data-centre diversification adds a capital-efficient, recurring-revenue stream to an otherwise lumpy developer business
key_risks: ROIC remains sub-Magic-Formula territory at ROCE 11.2% — real estate capital intensity structurally limits returns on deployed capital
OCF is erratic (3/5 years positive, including a -26 Cr year in 2024) as real estate cash flows are lumpy and project-dependent
Earnings yield of ~2.6% leaves no margin of safety at P/E 35x; deceleration in residential sales or data-centre delays would reprice sharply
red_flags: ROCE of 11.2% and ROE of 10.9% are both well below the Magic Formula's 20% threshold — capital is not being deployed at attractive returns
Capex rose to INR 77 Cr in 2025, and cumulative FCF over 5 years is barely positive — asset-heavy model absorbs most earnings
Real estate revenue recognition is policy-dependent; high P/S of 7.7x implies market is pricing the land bank, not near-term earnings
analysis.detailed_analysis: The Magic Formula ranks Anant Raj as mediocre on both dimensions. Earnings yield of ~2.6% is far too low — I want 12%+ — and ROCE of 11.2% is below the 20% floor I use for business quality. The improving P&L is real and driven by genuine volume recovery plus interest cost reduction, but the deployed capital base is very large (total assets INR 5,446 Cr vs. EBITDA INR 529 Cr), which structurally caps ROIC in real estate development. The data-centre optionality is interesting and could eventually push ROIC higher, but it is not yet visible in the financial returns.
